 Order
% 27.03.2026 Crl.M.A. 9185/2026 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Petitioner seeks setting aside of order dated 02.12.2025 of learned trial court and quashing of FIR No. 2/2025 of PS Moti Nagar for offence under Section 420/468/471 IPC.

3. Broadly speaking, the complainant de facto alleged that the accused/applicant committed forgery of title documents dated 08.12.1997 by fabricating signatures of one Mr. U.C. Bhatia, whereas Mr.
Bhatia had allegedly passed away in the year 1983 itself.

On the basis of these limited allegations,
the local police was directed to conduct enquiry and file a report This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/03/2026 at 22:55:08 in response to application under Section 175(3) BNSS.
In the name of enquiry, the IO simply recorded statement of daughter of Mr. Bhatia.

No effort was done by the IO to obtain death certificate of Mr. Bhatia and on the said material, the learned trial court passed the impugned order,
thereby allowing the application under Section 175(3) BNSS.
Consequently, the subject FIR got registered.
4. Learned APP accepts notice and seeks and is allowed two weeks to file status report.
5. Learned counsel for respondent no.2 (complainant de facto) also accepts notice.
6. The IO Tasvir Mathur has not appeared.
Even the SHO concerned has not cared to appear.
SI Amit Kumar present in court is not aware as regards the date when status report was filed without even collecting death certificate of Mr. Bhatia.

As repeatedly directed in number of cases, this also Kusum vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194843348/
1 appears to be yet another case of complete lethargy (if not deliberate inaction) on the part of police.
